## TL;DR

This change adds a dev-only Android update channel for RepoOS Hub, an on-demand publisher, a Cloudflare Worker that protects and serves channel files with noindex headers, and a main-branch workflow that publishes after pushes once its secrets are configured. The mobile release bundle guard passed, the mobile Vue/TypeScript release build passed, and `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed. The Cloudflare account setup, first live publication, and physical-phone install/upgrade remain unverified and are tracked by held human task #1158.

## Work and rationale

I inspected the Android Gradle variants, the Capacitor app shell, Settings, the mobile dependencies, the existing adb deploy recipe, and the relevant build commands. The Hub app did not already have an update checker. I kept this in the existing Vue/Capacitor shell and reused Capacitor Preferences for hourly check/snooze state and the installed browser plugin to open the APK URL for Android's download/install handling.

The update check is enabled only on Android when the dev package ID and a nonempty dev channel URL are compiled into the bundle. The publisher injects the URL, commit, version code, and package ID into the debug web bundle before Gradle assembles the debug APK. Release builds receive none of those values. The check compares numeric version codes, displays the available commit and notes, remains silent on failure, and lets the user snooze for one hour. Settings displays the build commit and offers Check now only when the dev channel is enabled.

`scripts/publish-dev.sh` builds the existing `.dev` Android variant and writes a manifest with version name/code, commit, build time, and recent commit subjects as short notes. It uploads the APK and manifest to the private R2 bucket. `just publish-dev` supports local manual publication while preserving `just deploy-phone` as the adb fallback.

The Worker in `mobile/dev-update-worker/` serves only GET/HEAD requests for the two tokenized channel objects, rejects other paths, and adds `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, noarchive`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. This keeps bucket contents private from listing and avoids exposing a public unguessable URL through the RepoOS site. The main-branch workflow deploys the Worker and publishes the latest debug APK after pushes once the required Cloudflare and channel secrets are configured.

The release-channel guard builds the mobile web bundle with channel variables removed and fails if the host or configured token appears in its output. I ran it with a harmless probe token; the release bundle compiled and the scan passed. The worker, local publisher, setup guide, and automation are described in `docs/hub-android-dev-updates.md`.

I filed held human task #1158 for Cloudflare bucket/domain setup and secret creation. Its purpose is to keep account-owned provisioning out of source changes and make the external dependency explicit.

## Approaches tried

I searched for an existing mobile update implementation first. The repository's other update checker belongs to the RepoOS CLI/web app and does not fit the native Hub, so reusing it would have coupled different products. The Hub already includes Capacitor Preferences and InAppBrowser, so no new runtime dependency was needed.

I first attempted to use Capacitor's browser API as `Browser.open`; the installed package exports `InAppBrowser.openInExternalBrowser`. The local mobile release build caught this mismatch. After correcting it, `scripts/check-mobile-release-channel.sh` ran `vue-tsc` and Vite successfully. I also moved the channel gate from URL-only to URL plus the debug package ID so an accidental URL value alone does not activate the update flow.

## Challenges and blockers

No Cloudflare credentials or domain control were available in this session. The Worker route, bucket binding, and secret have not been deployed against the live account, and no live `X-Robots-Tag` response was observed. The main-branch workflow has not run with configured secrets, so no claim is made that an APK or manifest has been published.

No Android phone was available. Android package-signature continuity, install-over-existing behavior, app-data preservation, reachability on mobile data, and prompt behavior remain unverified. The setup document describes verification; human task #1158 covers account setup, but the actual phone evidence still needs to be supplied by Nick.

The first mobile build attempt ran before mobile dependencies were installed and reported missing Capacitor packages. I installed the declared mobile dependencies in this worktree, fixed the browser-plugin import, and reran the mobile release-bundle build successfully. No live channel token was generated or printed in this session.

## Key learnings

The debug application ID suffix is already established in Gradle, and Vite build-time variables provide a clean way to embed the private channel only in the dev bundle. Android version ordering must use the numeric version code, not the display version or commit string. A tokenized URL still needs a server-side gate and robots header; a public R2 custom domain alone would not enforce the requested response behavior. Finally, build and CI configuration can be completed in code, but Cloudflare provisioning and real device upgrade proof remain separate human-owned steps.
